scope: Bounded external-source research for repository governance in an AI-assisted development workflow: agent-facing repository guidance, GitHub issue/PR intake templates, and architectural decision record ownership and lifecycle. This is evidence for parent-owned adjudication, not a local policy decision.

search_accounting.count_definition: The 15 requested search-result slots are discovery volume, not validated source count. Four distinct source pages were selected, fetched, and directly checked; duplicate results and additional candidates were not retained.

searches.query: Official AGENTS.md documentation describing the open cross-agent repository instruction format, README relationship, nested path-specific guidance, and scope.
Official GitHub Docs explaining repository issue templates and pull request templates, their storage locations, configurable fields, and how templates guide contributors.
An established official ADR process guide specifying ADR owner responsibilities, proposal/review/acceptance/rejection status, immutability, and superseding records.

search_accounting.verification: Pages were fetched with Exa and opened directly in the browser. The cross-check did not add source documents beyond the four listed below.

sources.title: AGENTS.md
sources.publisher: AGENTS.md project; the page states stewardship by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation
sources.revision_or_date: Current live page; no stable revision/date displayed
observed: AGENTS.md is ordinary Markdown for repository-specific coding-agent context and instructions, including setup, tests, conventions, and security considerations.
The page presents AGENTS.md as complementary to human-facing README files and describes root and nested instructions for projects and subprojects.
It does not prescribe required fields.
sources.application_inference: Keep the root agent entry concise and durable: repository boundaries, how to start, and links to current contracts or evidence. Put subject-specific detail in the owning documents and use pointers to support progressive disclosure.
limits: The page describes the format's intended use, not a measured guarantee that instructions will always be read or followed.
Its reported adoption count is a publisher statement and was not independently measured here.
An instruction file is not a transcript archive, issue tracker, roadmap, decision log, or evidence of user authorization.

sources.title: Configuring issue templates for your repository
observed: Issue templates and forms can shape contributor input; issue forms support structured fields such as text, dropdowns, checkboxes, and uploads.
Issue forms live in `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE`; the template chooser can enable or disable blank issues and route some reports to contact links.
Templates become available to contributors after they are merged into the repository's default branch. The page marks issue forms as public preview.
sources.application_inference: Use an issue template to request a stable problem statement, reproduction/evidence links, scope, and impact. Keep the submitted GitHub issue as the platform record and link it from the local execution or research record; the form does not itself adjudicate or accept the request.
limits: This describes GitHub's issue intake mechanism, not a universal issue lifecycle or records-retention policy.
The documentation does not cover roadmaps, architecture decisions, agent Explore reports, human chat transcripts, or repository disclosure of private inputs.

sources.title: Creating a pull request template for your repository
observed: A pull request template pre-populates the PR body and can ask for a related issue, a description of proposed changes, and reviewers.
Templates can be placed in supported root, `docs/`, or `.github/` paths; multiple templates can be selected through a template query parameter.
The template becomes available after merge to the default branch.
sources.application_inference: Use the PR body for a concise candidate-change summary, exact related ticket/decision IDs, verification evidence, and reviewers. Keep the live PR's status and review state authoritative; the local handoff should link to the actual PR and commit rather than label a local plan as a GitHub PR.
limits: A template is a submission scaffold, not a durable decision log or release receipt.
The page does not define when a PR or issue should be mirrored or archived outside GitHub.

sources.title: Architectural decision record process
sources.source_type: Official vendor process guide; mature ADR practice example
observed: An ADR records an architecturally significant choice, its context, and consequences; a collection forms a decision log whose headings help readers orient before opening details.
The guide assigns an ADR owner who maintains and communicates the record; other team members may contribute.
The lifecycle distinguishes proposed, accepted, and rejected decisions; after acceptance or rejection the record is treated as immutable, and a later accepted ADR supersedes the previous one.
sources.application_inference: Separate source-backed Explore from the decision owner's canonical ruling. For significant decisions, record the owner, status, context, decision, consequences, links to the inputs and implementation record, and any superseding decision; retain prior accepted/rejected records as history.
limits: This is AWS's recommended ADR process, not a universal standard or a mandate to turn every product choice, issue, or user message into an ADR.
It does not specify how to archive ChatGPT sessions, raw user messages, roadmaps, design assets, or privacy-sensitive evidence.

cross_source_inferences: The sources support different record jobs: AGENTS.md provides predictable agent instructions; GitHub templates structure new issue/PR submissions; an ADR records an owned, reviewable decision. Combining these into one growing file would blur their owners and lifecycle.

The sources do not provide a shared external standard for roadmaps, intermediate multi-agent Explore notes, user-session transcripts, human user messages, or local design references. Their disposition must come from CourtWork's own contracts and explicit user choice.
The sources support discoverable entrypoints and linked detail, but do not justify automatically loading raw archives into every agent context or publishing private source material.
research_limits: This is a four-document source check, not a survey or frequency study of repository practice.
GitHub's documentation establishes platform behavior, not the repository's actual issue/PR state.
No tools, schemas, archive policy, retention period, or framework were selected by this research.
